newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CNP/NPM takes steps to lower NAV discount.
newsitem.headline: CNP/NPM takes steps to lower NAV discount.

text.p: Belgian holding company Cie Nationale a Portefeuille /Nationale Portefeuillemaatschappij said in its annual report to shareholders it would publish a weekly estimate of its net asset value from May 31 in an effort to narrow the discount between its share price and real value.
The company said it would publish the information in Belgium's leading financial papers as well as a new website: http://www.cnp.be.

"This weekly estimated value will be determined based on the same criteria used to determine the estimated value published in the annual reports. However, certain simplifying assumptions will be made," it said. Operations which impact the portfolio by less than one percent will not be included.
At April 30, 1997, when the annual report went to press, the NAV of the company was approximately 3,150 francs a share, it said. At 1200 GMT on Friday the share was at 2,600 francs.
In 1996, measures to narrow the discount included the purchase of 479,869, or 1.89 percent, of its own shares for a value of 872 million Belgian francs.
CNP/NPM used its annual report to set out in detail the company's objectives and position within the group of companies controlled by Belgian businessman Albert Frere and his family.

It also launched a defence of the way it was governed, noting its board was "balanced", including five independent directors. This follows statements made by Frere at the annual general meeting of his Groupe Bruxelles Lambert at which he attacked Belgian government corporate governance plans.
CNP/NPM owns 47.8 percent of GBL through its Parjointco joint venture with Canada's Desmarais family-controlled Power Corp.

The Belgian government has proposed creating a new company statute, the "autonomous company", which balances controlling shareholders interests against those of minority shareholders by forcing boards to include independent directors.
"If this new structure were imposed on GBL or its subsidiaries we would have to react categorically," GBL co-chairman Jean-Pierre de Launoit told GBL's annual shareholders meeting earlier this week.
CNP/NPM is due to hold its annual shareholders meeting on June 11 at its new headquarters in Loverval near Charleroi.
